evals.prompt: Create a Throughline Markdown visualization of a request moving from a client to a server, with an initial empty response, a visible transfer, then a response update. Include code to compile it.
evals.expected_output: Uses thl flow, predeclares nodes/links, creates distinct explanatory beats, uses send for transfer and set for state mutation, compiles one block, and inspects state across frames.

evals.prompt: Use Throughline to show what happens when two variables alias an array and one pushes a value, then rebinds. Write the shortest supported example and explain its limitations.
evals.expected_output: Uses thl bindings with supported let/const, reference assignments and push; explains shared object semantics and that const immutability and arbitrary JavaScript are not enforced.

evals.prompt: Embed a thl matrix code fence with a live Throughline player next to the source in my React 19/Fumadocs MDX docs. Make it work for multiple fences in one page.
evals.expected_output: Explains MDX host extraction, compiles each block independently at build/server time, uses exact root/react/CSS imports, passes Trace to a client wrapper, and does not claim MDX fences auto-render.

evals.prompt: Visualize Fibonacci recursion with thl callstack and pass source directly to ThroughlinePlayer with autoplay.
evals.expected_output: Rejects nonexistent Fibonacci callstack support and source/autoplay props; uses thl flow to hand-author the concept if appropriate, compile(source) separately, and render ThroughlinePlayer with the compiled trace.

evals.prompt: Debug this Throughline flow where a packet is sent on a hidden link, and I write both x and x[0] in one step. Show a corrected timeline.
evals.expected_output: Identifies hidden topology and overlapping writes as compile errors, shows link/node visibility before transfer, splits conflicting writes, and validates the revised flow.
